PullRequest.Title: fix: race activateByEvent with provider registration to prevent auth deadlock
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #315841

When connecting to a remote tunnel, the webworker extension host can deadlock waiting for `_installedExtensionsReady` (which requires a remote connection), while the remote connection needs auth. Previously, `tryActivateProvider` exclusively awaited `activateByEvent`, blocking until all extension hosts responded.

Fix by `Promise.race`-ing `activateByEvent` against the auth provider registering itself. This allows the local process extension host to deliver the provider and unblock auth without waiting for a stuck webworker host.

fyi @TylerLeonhardt -- there is now a race between the `activateByEvent` promise and the provider registering. This avoids deadlocks in a certain scenario where there are web worker extensions installed on the desktop.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: An all-extension-host activation barrier was placed before observing successful authentication-provider registration, so one blocked host could indefinitely hold the tunnel authentication and connection critical path even after another host had supplied the provider.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Connecting to a remote tunnel can deadlock indefinitely while obtaining cached authentication sessions when the local webworker extension host is blocked on remote authority setup.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The changed code starts activation but races its aggregate promise against the provider-registration event, then reads the provider map immediately. Tunnel authentication can therefore continue as soon as any host registers the requested provider, without waiting for an unrelated blocked host; host activation itself remains cached and continues in the background.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before this PR, AuthenticationService.tryActivateProvider awaited activateByEvent before checking the provider map. AbstractExtensionService._activateByEvent returns Promise.all over the selected extension-host managers, each manager crosses its extension-host proxy via activateByEvent. The remote-tunnel connect critical path calls _getTokenForProvider -> AuthenticationService.getSessions(..., activateImmediate=true) before it can call the tunnel main service. A local process host can register MainThreadAuthenticationProvider and fire onDidRegisterAuthenticationProvider while a local webworker host's activation remains blocked; the added test reproduces that aggregate activation promise never settling despite successful provider registration.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connect to a remote tunnel using GitHub or Microsoft authentication while a local webworker extension host is blocked during remote-authority setup.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: TunnelAgentHostService.connect waits for _getToken/_getTokenForProvider, which waits for AuthenticationService.getSessions and cold-provider activation before _mainService.connect and protocol setup can begin. After the diff, provider registration from the local process host releases this path even if the aggregate activation promise remains blocked.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the authentication activation event to each selected extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold path: one effective proxy activation per selected host manager and provider activation event; manager-level promise caching coalesces concurrent duplicate requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same activation IPC fan-out occurred, but AuthenticationService exclusively awaited its Promise.all result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously all selected hosts had to settle before AuthenticationService could observe an already registered provider. The diff lets provider registration remove that aggregate IPC barrier while activation continues.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query exact-scope sessions and optionally all sessions from the registered extension-host authentication provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query per attempted provider, plus one fallback query only when the exact-scope result is empty; provider attempts are sequential.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same session RPCs ran only after aggregate activation completed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These calls remain on the token-acquisition critical path after provider activation/registration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connect the authenticated tunnel and establish its protocol client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One tunnel connect and one protocol connection for a successful user connection attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A blocked extension-host activation could prevent this boundary from being reached indefinitely.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This work starts only after token acquisition; the diff can unblock reaching it sooner.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most the configured GitHub and Microsoft providers are attempted sequentially; each provider can perform an exact-scope session query and, only when empty, one all-sessions fallback. Cold activation fans out to the selected extension-host managers, while the effective IPC cardinality is one cached activation per provider event per host manager.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Providers and exact/all session queries are sequential. Extension-host activation is concurrent via Promise.all, but the changed Promise.race no longer makes every host's completion a barrier. ExtensionHostManager caches each activation-event promise, so concurrent callers do not multiply extension-host IPC for the same host/event.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A registered provider is a warm map hit and skips tryActivateProvider entirely. On a cold provider, each host manager caches the activation event; the registration event is the new early completion signal. There is no negative provider cache, and a completed activation without registration retains the existing five-second wait.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: getSessions is directly on tunnel connection's critical path, activation is a Promise.all over extension hosts, and the test proves registration can occur while that promise never resolves.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of the blocked-webworker configuration and wall-clock delay varies, but the indefinite barrier and its removal are directly established by the call path and regression test.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression. The change removes an all-host latency barrier without increasing effective boundary cardinality; it is recorded as a regression fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: An extension or workbench action gets/creates sessions for an authentication provider that is not yet registered.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: getSessions/createSession waits for tryActivateProvider, then invokes the provider RPC. The diff races activation completion with registration; if activation completes first without registration, the existing five-second registration timeout still applies.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate the provider extension in selected extension hosts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One effective activation IPC per selected host manager for a cold provider event; duplicate requests reuse manager-cached promises.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: AuthenticationService awaited all selected hosts before checking registration or beginning the timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff shortens the wait when registration arrives before all hosts settle and otherwise preserves the prior activation-plus-timeout path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Get or create authentication sessions through the extension-host provider proxy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider RPC for the requested operation after successful registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider RPC followed activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Unchanged and remains after provider readiness.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One provider ID per request. getOrActivateProviderIdForServer can examine the filtered set of matching, unregistered declared providers sequentially; that loop and its candidate cardinality are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Activation fans out concurrently to selected extension hosts. Concurrent requests can each hold a registration listener, but the underlying host activation is cached per event/manager; listeners are disposed in tryActivateProvider's finally block as soon as each request completes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm provider-map hits avoid activation. Cold activation is coalesced by ExtensionHostManager's event cache. No new persistent cache or negative cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: listener ownership, activation caching, and all completion branches are visible in the implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of concurrent cold requests is workload-dependent, but each added listener is bounded by an in-flight call and synchronously registered providers are caught by the map check; disposal is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Temporary listener lifetime is bounded, effective IPC count is unchanged, and the main behavioral change reduces cold-path latency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Traced authentication activation through extension-host IPC, provider RPC, and the remote-tunnel connection path; checked warm/cold provider state, activation coalescing, concurrency, timeout, cancellation, and listener disposal. No diff-introduced performance finding was found; the PR fixes a concrete boundary-fanout latency regression and that fix was recorded.
